```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This guide provisions one Brev L40S instance, builds the package-locked
BioNeMo Recipes Evo 2 image, and runs R on the host against that container.
The workflow is opt-in because it starts billable compute.

Two checks remain separate:

1. A quick smoke test verifies dense generation, scoring, and pooled
   embeddings.
2. The full acceptance capture adds fixed synthetic preprocessing, two BF16
   rank-4 LoRA optimizer steps, and fitted scoring and generation.

The scripts upload an existing MBridge checkpoint. They do not test or claim
checkpoint conversion.

## Inspect before provisioning

The provisioning script performs a dry run by default:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-create.sh
```

Inspect the current Brev catalog and price, then request the exact instance:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-create.sh --create bionemor-evo2
```

There is no GPU-type fallback.

## Run the quick smoke test

The build script requires an existing 7B MBridge checkpoint under the remote
workspace:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
brev copy ./ bionemor-evo2:/home/ubuntu/bionemor/
brev exec bionemor-evo2 \
  "mkdir -p /home/ubuntu/bionemor-workspace/checkpoints/evo2-7b"
brev copy /path/to/evo2-7b/ \
  bionemor-evo2:/home/ubuntu/bionemor-workspace/checkpoints/evo2-7b/
brev exec bionemor-evo2 \
  "BIONEMOR_EVO2_CHECKPOINT=/home/ubuntu/bionemor-workspace/checkpoints/evo2-7b bash /home/ubuntu/bionemor/inst/scripts/brev-evo2-recipes.sh"
```

The script checks out the locked upstream source, verifies the official Evo 2
Dockerfile, binds its base image to the release-lock digest, appends the
package helper, and builds the image. It then installs the R package, verifies
the uploaded checkpoint, and runs the quick inference smoke.

Stop an instance after a manual run:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
brev stop bionemor-evo2
```

## Capture the full public-API workflow

The explicit runner provisions the instance, uploads the checkpoint and
package source, runs both checks, copies the completed evidence locally, and
stops the instance from an `EXIT` trap:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
BIONEMOR_EVO2_CHECKPOINT_SOURCE=/path/to/evo2-7b \
  ./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-run.sh --run bionemor-evo2
```

The acceptance script uses fixed 127-base synthetic inputs. Preprocessing
appends the end-of-document token to produce 128-token samples. It checks dense
score, generation, and embeddings; runs two LoRA steps; then checks fitted
score and generation. Seeded generation is checked for shape and token count,
not exact generated bases.

Evidence is published only after every operation and assertion succeeds. The
runner copies a bounded record to `validation/brev-evo2/<date>/` before
stopping the instance:

- full-precision summary JSON;
- compact dense and fitted outputs;
- redacted terminal manifests;
- retained LoRA inspection metadata.

It does not copy checkpoints, weight shards, tensors, container images, logs,
or complete workspaces. A capture records one mechanical synthetic workflow;
it is not a benchmark or a biological-quality evaluation. No dated capture is
checked in until this opt-in workflow completes successfully.

NIM is not used by either check.
